To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Co(OH) 2-based supercapactor electrode composed of sucker-like nanoporous film grown on the nickel foam exhibits a remarkable performance with a specific capacitance of 850 F/g in a two electrode configuration at 20 A/ g in the potential window of 1.4 V, which is the best result reported for the Co(OH)(2)-based supercapacitor electrode in a two electrode system.

the large specific capacitance of the Co(OH) 2 electrodes was attributed to the synergistic effect of the large surface area and the high conversion of Co oxidation states during the charge/discharging process.

the Co(OH) 2 nanoporous electrodes were fabricated by a facile electrochemical deposition and the remarkable performance of Co(OH)(2) nanoporous films were correlated with a large redox conversion of the Co(2+) to Co(4+) during the charge-discharge cycling.
